events.title: First Battle of St Albans
events.description: Yorkist forces clashed with the Lancastrian royal army in the streets of St Albans, north of London. The fighting lasted about an hour, and the Yorkists won decisively.
events.significance: It is widely regarded as the opening battle of the Wars of the Roses, the dynastic struggle that convulsed England for decades.

events.title: SS Savannah Sets Out Across the Atlantic
events.description: The SS Savannah left port in Savannah, Georgia, on a voyage to Liverpool. It was a sailing ship fitted with a steam engine and paddle wheels.
events.significance: It became the first steamship to cross the Atlantic, an early step toward the age of steam-powered ocean travel.

events.title: Abraham Lincoln Receives a Patent
events.description: Lincoln was issued a patent for a device to lift boats over river shoals and obstacles. He had come up with the idea from his own experience on river boats.
events.significance: Lincoln remains the only U.S. president to have held a patent.

events.title: Wright Brothers Granted Flying-Machine Patent
events.description: The U.S. Patent Office granted Orville and Wilbur Wright patent number 821,393 for their "Flying-Machine." The patent covered their method of controlling an aircraft.
events.significance: The patent recognized the brothers' breakthrough in aircraft control and became central to the early history of aviation.

events.title: Great Chilean Earthquake
events.description: A huge rupture off the coast near Valdivia, Chile, struck in the afternoon. It produced a quake of magnitude 9.5.
events.significance: It is the strongest earthquake ever recorded by instruments, and its tsunami caused damage across the Pacific.
